newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rescues 858 Albanians from grounded ship.
newsitem.headline: Italy rescues 858 Albanians from grounded ship.

text.p: Italian coastguards said on Sunday they had rescued 858 Albanian refugees, including a heavily pregnant woman and a new-born baby, from a ship that ran aground off the port of Brindisi.
Another 317 Albanians fleeing the anarchy in the Balkan state arrived during the night at the larger Italian port of Bari further to the north on three fishing boats.

A Reuter correspondent who watched the all-night rescue operation in Brindisi from one of several coastguard vessels alongside said the Albanian navy patrol ship's deck was heaving with people. Some were waving white flags.

The ancient patrol boat, carrying the number F324, ran aground several hundred metres off the shore in shallow water within sight of a petrochemical complex as it was being escorted into port after crossing the Adriatic sea.

Coastguards in the southern port said that four of their ships, a navy patrol boat and other smaller vessels worked throughout the night in ferrying the refugees from the ship to harbour in seas that grew rough as the hours passed.
The operation was completed after daybreak on Sunday and the Albanians given medical treatment and food.
An Italian helicopter had hovered over the ship with a searchlight scanning the sea, in case any of the Albanians had jumped in, but there were no reports of casualties.

"The crews were excellent. Working in that sea to save all those people, and in the shallows, and without anyone being injured, was exceptional," said Giovanni Biso, the chief of the Brindisi coastguard operations.
"They were piled one on top of each other, on a boat no longer than 50 metres and this increased the risks of the rescue," he told reporters in Brindisi.
"Fortunately now the seas are picking up and we hope that maybe that will be enough to halt the exodus."
Thousands of Albanians have been streaming across the Adriatic sea in a ramshackle fleet of decrepit boats since violence broke out in the country this month.
Italy has said the refugees will be given political asylum but will be repatriated once the anarchy subsided.
